rfm_tuples.R: Tripadvisor is an 'experiences-led' marketplace; the Experiences + TheFork marketplaces 'accounted for approximately 60% of consolidated revenue mix and 35% of consolidated adjusted EBITDA' in FY25, up from 50%/6% in FY23 — framed as the long-term value-creation engine.
rfm_tuples.f: If true and accelerating, post-cutoff Q1 2026 disclosure should reaffirm Experiences segment growth AND show improving segment-level profitability (or at least not deterioration).
rfm_tuples.M_source: claim_evolution.query_claim_evolution(cik='0001526520', search_term='Experiences segment', base_filing_date='2026-02-13', cutoff='2026-05-20') + Q1 2026 8-K earnings release (5/7/26) segment table.
rfm_tuples.M_value: claim_evolution: REAFFIRMED_IN_STRUCTURED_DISCLOSURE (10-Q + 8-K mentions, no termination). Q1 2026 segment data: Experiences revenue $167.9M (+8% YoY) BUT Experiences Adjusted EBITDA WORSENED to -$19.2M from -$14.1M (loss grew 36%). TheFork revenue $57.3M (+23%), TheFork EBITDA flipped positive to $4.6M from -$3.5M. Hotels & Other Adjusted EBITDA fell 40% to $36.7M from $61.4M. The 'Experiences-led' segment is growing topline but its absolute EBITDA loss is widening — the segment that's supposed to fund the re-rate is consuming more cash, not less.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mix-shift narrative is technically reaffirmed (Experiences + TheFork are growing share of revenue) but the EBITDA economics of the lead segment are deteriorating intra-year, and the high-margin Hotels & Other segment that subsidizes the mix shift is contracting -22% constant currency. The transition is real but the unit-economic bridge to profitability is widening, not closing.

rfm_tuples.f: If genuinely partnership-based and material, the megacap counterparty (Booking Holdings) should reciprocally disclose Tripadvisor in its own SEC filings at a meaningful cadence.

rfm_tuples.R: Capital-return discipline — $250M share-repurchase authorization (Sep 2023), with $110M still remaining at 12/31/25; in 2025 the Company repurchased 6.1M shares at $14.72 avg ($90M total) AND retired 26.8M LTRIP shares at $16.28 ($437M).
rfm_tuples.f: If true and counter-cyclically deployed, with TRIP at -47% drawdown and stock near 52w low through Q1 2026, the Company should be actively using the remaining $110M authorization at trough prices.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 10-Q explicitly: 'During the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company did NOT repurchase any shares of outstanding common stock under the share repurchase program.' Buyback program is FROZEN both periods despite $110M still available and stock trading near 52-week low (closing Q1 around $11). The $437M LTRIP-share retirement (Apr 2025) was a one-off Merger-related transaction at $16.28, not an open-market trough buy. Open-market authorization is sitting on the sidelines through one of the deepest drawdowns in TRIP's history.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'capital-return discipline' framing is technically true (authorization exists, dollars deployed in 2024) but in 2025 only $90M was spent at $14.72 avg, and in Q1 2026 — at the literal trough — ZERO buybacks were executed despite $110M of unused authorization. Management is preserving cash for the August 2026 convertible-notes redemption rather than supporting the stock at $11. That's prudent treasury behavior, but it directly contradicts the implied counter-cyclical buyback thesis that small-cap rebound investors rely on. The signal is: management is preparing for the maturity wall, not supporting the equity floor.

rfm_tuples.R: Q4 2025 restructuring (~$33M severance, ~$4M expected in Q1 2026) realigned operations from Viator/Brand Tripadvisor segments into the new Experiences/Hotels-Other/TheFork structure — framed as positioning for AI-led growth and operating leverage. Cost savings 'expected to begin to be realized in 2026 and fully realized by 2027.'
rfm_tuples.f: If genuinely productive, post-cutoff Q1 2026 results should show some early opex leverage and improving segment margins.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 Total Adjusted EBITDA $22.1M vs Q1 2025 $43.8M — DOWN 50% YoY. Adj EBITDA margin compressed to 5.8% from 11.0% YoY. Hotels & Other Adj EBITDA -40% YoY ($36.7M from $61.4M). Experiences Adj EBITDA LOSS WIDENED from -$14.1M to -$19.2M (-36%). TheFork is the only positive surprise (flipped from -$3.5M to +$4.6M). The restructuring savings have NOT yet shown up in segment economics — the high-margin legacy segment is shrinking faster than the new-segment unit economics are improving.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'cost savings + AI-led repositioning' narrative is contradicted by the first post-restructuring quarter: Adj EBITDA is HALVED, not improved. Either the restructuring savings are back-end-loaded (consistent with 'fully realized by 2027' language) or the legacy-segment erosion is outpacing them. Investors paying the multiple for the rebound have to underwrite a savings curve that the first quarter post-restructuring did not validate.

rfm_tuples.f: If true, the public float should expand, voting structure should be 1-share-1-vote, and the structural overhang from Liberty's 56% voting block should be eliminated cleanly.

summary: TripAdvisor passes the universal-quality screens cleanly: KPMG-clean audit, no going-concern language, $1.12B cash vs $345M August-2026 convertible (3.2x coverage), simplified post-LTRIP cap structure, customer-concentration trending DOWN (Booking+Expedia 25% -> 21% over three years), insider activity routine and small ($4.4M/yr, all 10b5-1 or tax-withhold), and Booking/Expedia both reciprocally namecheck TRIP in their own filings (8 + 42 hits respectively) — the partnership claim is genuine. The two SEVERE markdowns are: (1) BUYBACK FREEZE — zero open-market repurchases in Q1 2025 OR Q1 2026 despite $110M remaining authorization and stock at 52w low, signaling management is preserving cash for the August convertible-notes redemption rather than supporting the floor; and (2) RESTRUCTURING SAVINGS NOT YET VISIBLE — Q1 2026 Adj EBITDA halved YoY ($22.1M vs $43.8M, -50%), Experiences segment EBITDA loss widened ($-19.2M vs $-14.1M), Hotels & Other EBITDA -40%. The MODERATE markdown is the Experiences-led mix-shift narrative being topline-real (Q1 Experiences +8% revenue, TheFork +23%) but unit-economic-deteriorating (lead segment burns more cash, not less). Net: TRIP is solvent, transparent, and structurally cleaning up — but the post-cutoff Q1 print materially weakens the rebound thesis. Composite 1.000 on the small-cap honesty-alpha rubric = honest disclosure of a softening operator, not a fraud setup. LONG-able only if you can underwrite the 2027 restructuring-savings curve and tolerate flat-to-down Hotels & Other through 2026.
